description: Search the Drugs@FDA database for drug application approvals (NDAs and ANDAs). Returns application details, sponsor info, and full submission history. Pair with openfda_get_drug_label to read the approved label, or openfda_count_values to aggregate by sponsor_name, product_type, or route. With stage=true, call openfda_dataframe_describe for the staged columns, then openfda_dataframe_query for SQL.

canvas_id.description: Canvas ID returned by a prior stage=true call to this tool or another openFDA search tool (openfda_search_* or openfda_lookup_ndc). Passing one stages this search onto that canvas (same effect as stage=true) so result sets accumulate for cross-table joins. Omit to stage onto a fresh canvas.

fields.description: Dotted record paths to keep on each returned record, e.g. ["sponsor_name", "submissions.submission_status_date"] — any key path on a returned record works, and openfda_describe_fields lists the searchable ones. Each record is projected to these paths plus its identity key (application_number), identically on both response surfaces, and a path through an array applies to every element. Use it when records are large: when a record on the page serializes above 24000 bytes, page_bytes reports the page's size and page_largest_fields names the largest record's biggest fields. A path no returned record carries is named on the notice. Omit for whole records. Paths take only letters, digits, underscores, and dots; anything else is rejected before the request. With stage=true, only the inline page is projected — the staged table keeps its columns.

limit.description: Records per page. A record carries its application's whole submission history, so a long-running application is an order of magnitude larger than a recent one. Default 25; a larger value returns at most 375 and says so.

search.description: openFDA search query. Examples: products.brand_name:"eliquis" (any letter case; openfda.* fields are filled only on harmonized applications, so openfda.brand_name misses the rest), sponsor_name:"PFIZER", submissions.submission_type:"ORIG" AND submissions.review_priority:"PRIORITY". Exact quoted values can be case-sensitive on some fields — sponsor_name is stored uppercase, so use sponsor_name:"PFIZER" (a lowercase quoted value returns no matches). Omit to browse by latest submission, newest first, sorted by submissions.submission_status_date:desc. Separate clauses with spaces. A "+" written in the URL style of openFDA's examples also reads as a space where it separates: beside AND, OR, NOT, or TO, after a closing quote, paren, or bracket, or between a term and the next "field:" prefix (a:"x"+AND+b:"y", [20200101+TO+20201231], c:x+d:y). In a query that marks a clause required with a leading +field:, only the AND/OR/NOT/TO positions read that way. Any other "+" is sent as written, and inside a quoted phrase "+" is a literal plus sign. Double quotes, parentheses, and range brackets must balance, and the query must not end on a backslash — each is rejected before the request.

skip.description: Number of records to skip for pagination (default 0). openFDA caps pagination at 25000 records; a higher value returns a pagination_limit_reached error.

sort.description: Sort expression — a field path optionally suffixed with :asc or :desc (any letter case; :ascending and :descending are also accepted, and every direction is sent as asc or desc); comma-separate for multi-field sort. Omitted with no search, defaults to submissions.submission_status_date:desc: applications by their latest submission status date, supplements included, newest first — not by approval date. Omitted with a search, results come in openFDA's relevance order. Field paths take only letters, digits, underscores, and dots; any other character or direction is rejected before the request. A well-formed but non-sortable field still causes a query error — use a documented field name.

stage.description: Stage the matched set on a DataCanvas for SQL analysis — openfda_dataframe_describe lists the staged columns, openfda_dataframe_query runs the SQL. Default false — the call returns one page for one upstream request. When true, records are also drained onto a canvas table up to a size budget (staged_rows reports how many reached it). Staging is for record-level SQL over a bounded slice; for a distribution over everything that matched, openfda_count_values aggregates server-side in one request. Requires CANVAS_PROVIDER_TYPE=duckdb.

name: openfda_search_drug_approvals

canvas_id.description: DataCanvas session id for the staged result set. Present when this call staged. Pass to openfda_dataframe_query / openfda_dataframe_describe, or back into this tool to accumulate more tables on the same canvas.

canvas_table.description: Canvas table holding the staged rows. Present when rows were staged; list its columns with openfda_dataframe_describe, then reference it in openfda_dataframe_query FROM clauses.

effectiveQuery.description: Search filter applied to the Drugs@FDA query, as submitted to openFDA

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `canvas_disabled`: Staging was requested (stage=true or a canvas_id) but DataCanvas is disabled. `canvas_not_found`: The canvas_id is well-formed but names no active canvas — expired or never minted. `canvas_capacity_exhausted`: canvas_id was omitted and the active canvas cap is already reached. `rate_limited`: The openFDA daily or per-minute request limit is exceeded. `upstream_error`: The openFDA API returned a 5xx server error. `malformed_search`: The search query leaves a double quote, parenthesis, or range bracket unclosed, or ends on a backslash. `query_error`: The search query was rejected by openFDA (malformed field name, invalid syntax). `pagination_limit_reached`: skip exceeds the 25000 record pagination ceiling. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

limit.description: Page size applied to this request: the requested limit, the endpoint default when limit was omitted, or the endpoint cap when limit exceeded it (the notice then says so). A window running past the end of the matched set returns fewer records than this, so read the length of results for the actual count.

totalUnverified.description: Present (true) only on an empty page at skip > 0 whose total could not be confirmed: openFDA answers a page past the end and a search that matched nothing alike, and the follow-up request for the total failed. total then reads 0 without ruling out records at a lower skip — re-call with skip=0 to tell.

notice.description: Canvas staging disclosure when the call staged, the limit clamp when limit exceeded the cap (requested value, cap, next skip), the fields projection and any requested path no record carries, the size and largest fields when a record on the page exceeds 24000 bytes, and guidance when results are empty — how to broaden filters or correct field names.

page_bytes.description: Serialized size of results in this response, in UTF-8 bytes. Present only when a record on the page serializes above 24000 bytes on its own — page_largest_fields then names the largest record's biggest fields, and fields projects each record to the paths you need.

page_largest_fields.description: Present with page_bytes: the biggest fields of the largest record on the page, largest first — the deepest single field that holds that record's excess over 24000 bytes, or else up to three top-level fields. Leave them out with a fields projection to shrink the records.

items.description: One field of the largest record and its serialized size.

bytes.description: Serialized UTF-8 bytes the field holds, totalled across array elements.

path.description: Dotted field path on the record. Fields of array elements share their array path, so patient.drug.openfda covers that block in every drug of the report.

projected_fields.description: The field paths each record in results was projected to, as requested — present only when the call passed fields. Every record also keeps its identity key; any other field is absent because the projection left it out, not because openFDA lacks it. Re-call without fields for whole records.

results.description: Drug application records — application_number, sponsor_name, openfda block on harmonized applications only (brand_name, generic_name, route, product_type, substance_name), products[] (brand_name, active_ingredients, dosage_form, marketing_status), submissions[] (submission_type, submission_status, submission_status_date, review_priority).

spilled.description: True when this call staged its matched set on the canvas — use canvas_id with openfda_dataframe_describe for its columns, then openfda_dataframe_query for SQL. Absent when staging was not requested.

staged_rows.description: Rows written to the canvas table. Compare with meta.total: a smaller value means staging stopped at its size budget or openFDA's 25000-row pagination ceiling, and the table holds only the first staged_rows records.

totalResults.description: Total matching drug approval records in the dataset

truncated.description: True when fewer rows reached the canvas than matched upstream — staging stopped at its size budget or openFDA's 25000-row pagination ceiling. Narrow the query (filters, date range) for a complete set.

title: Openfda Search Drug Approvals
